messages.author: 650fc680d9d7c1df
messages.subject: SQL backend for Teradata
parts:
I am in the process of trying to create a dplyr SQL backend for Teradata. 

Hadley's instructions here have helped me make good progress - and so far I have managed to get a connection to teradata and get a "meaningful description" back from the database.  One issue is that our enterprise TD system has thousands of tables so I think some mods to print() is required - but it does at least pull back the tables!

I am using RJDBC which implements most of the DBI methods you suggest need implementing - so far I have just relied on the DBI methods implemented as-is in RJDBC.

I have run into a problem when creating a tbl - the table exists (db_has_table returns TRUE) but I get an error "select is not a character vector" when trying to create the tbl object when calling tbl(), as below:

> db_has_table(s$con,"dw_users")
[1] TRUE
> t <- tbl(s,"dw_users")
Hide Traceback

Rerun with Debug
Error: select is not a character vector

9 assert_that(is.character(select), length(select) > 0L) at dbi-s3.r#195
8 sql_select.DBIConnection(x$src$con, from = from_sql, select = select_sql,
    where = where_sql, order_by = order_by_sql, group_by = group_by_sql,
    limit = limit) at dbi-s3.r#183
7 sql_select(x$src$con, from = from_sql, select = select_sql, where = where_sql,
    order_by = order_by_sql, group_by = group_by_sql, limit = limit) at tbl-sql.r#239
6 build_query(object) at tbl-sql.r#60
5 update.tbl_sql(tbl)
4 update(tbl) at tbl-sql.r#40
3 tbl_sql("teradata", src = src, from = from, ...) at src-teradata.R#48
2 tbl.src_teradata(s, "dw_users") at tbl.r#9
1 tbl(s, "dw_users")

Any pointers where I should go next? You can see my forked code in github here.

Thanks,
Matt

messages.subject: Re: SQL backend for Teradata
parts:
Hi Matt,

Two comments:

I made a whole lot of changes in the dev version, so I'd recommend getting that and reading the updated vignette. 

Jim Hester has been working on a generic jdbc backend which might be worth looking at/collaborating on. 

Also I never thought about the thousands of tables problem. Might need to tweak the default print method and provide some tools for listing tables that match a regular expression. 

Hadley

messages.author: 9855d5d5ac094e07
messages.subject: Re: SQL backend for Teradata
parts:
Hi Matt,

I'm not sure if you're still working on this or have now solved the problem. But I think you need to define the method "db_query_fields", otherwise in the "update.tbl_sql" (line 5), the function will return NULL for var_names in this snippet of code (https://github.com/hadley/dplyr/blob/master/R/tbl-sql.r, line ~53):

if (is.null(object$select)) {
var_names <- db_query_fields(object$src$con, object$from)
vars <- lapply(var_names, as.name)
object$select <- vars
}

This in turn will fail the "assert_that" portion since the select variable will be NULL not a character.


Hope it helps.

Chapman

Ok thanks for clarification. It would probably only be a little work forking the teradataR repo and making it DBI compliant (and hence a legitimate dplyr backend). 

If you want to start from scratch, Teradata have made available a JDBC driver (last updated Aug 2014) around which you can write a dplyr backend:

http://downloads.teradata.com/download/connectivity/jdbc-driver

There are other interfaces available here:

http://downloads.teradata.com/download/connectivity
